title: Muscle Loss is a Big Warning Sign of Dementia - Nautilus
gist: A new review finds sarcopenia, age-related muscle loss, may be a warning sign of dementia, while obesity has a more complicated relationship with the disease.

insights.claim: According to a new review, sarcopenia, the loss of muscle mass with age, may be a warning sign of dementia.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Supports muscle-preservation therapies and screening as dementia risk markers; relevant to muscle-sparing drug development.

insights.claim: Obesity has a more complicated relationship with dementia than muscle loss does.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Caution against simple weight-dementia narratives; watch for nuance in obesity-drug cognitive claims.
